The whole process of conceptualization is greatly aided and accelerated when the young child seriously begins to learn the language at 18 months.

During Stage Two, the child also learns to draw which means the child is becoming familiar with abstract symbols.


 What s that? is a common question that children in this stage ask. They are busy labeling all the objects in sight.�At this point, the child can understand the concepts of height and length, but not the concepts of mass or volume.�For example, the child will correctly answer the question,  Who is taller, you or your father? but he will be uncertain about which cake is bigger  one that is 23 cm by 23 cm or one that is 23 cm by 33 cm.

Another example: If four toy soldiers are grouped together and 4 toy soldiers are spaced a distance apart, the child might be inclined to say there are fewer toy soldiers in the first group.

In this stage, children use  make-believe as a tool for understanding and making sense of the adult world.
